contents.reason: Pointwise kernel limits away from or at the origin are not a commissioned claim or a proof prerequisite; concentration and initial-trace results are included separately.

contents.support: The library's convolution definition and its L^1 algebra properties are the published versions of these clauses.

contents.name: Proposition 1.1.1 (differentiating under the integral)

contents.support: The locally uniform initial convergence and C^∞ smoothing use the same kernel mechanism; the exponential-growth uniqueness class is deferred.

contents.name: Theorem 1.1 uniqueness in the exponential growth class (and Remark 1.1.3 on smoothing)
contents.reason: Uniqueness under an explicit growth bound is the recorded Gaussian-growth theorem of the PDE-8 pair; this pair proves representation and convergence only.

contents.name: Remark 1.1.4 (solutions spread over the entire space at any positive time)
Theorem 1.2 (Duhamel's principle via the fundamental solution)
contents.reason: Duhamel's principle is the commissioned central theorem of the PDE-8 pair and is deferred there rather than duplicated or consumed without proof here.

contents.name: §2 Lemma 2.0.2 (invariance under translation and parabolic dilation (2.0.22)–(2.0.24))

Theorem 1.1 and formula (1.1.12) (convolution representation and semigroup property)
contents.support: The kernel convolution identity Γ_t*Γ_s=Γ_{t+s} is the n-dimensional form of the semigroup computation used in the global Cauchy theorem; the local item proves it by completing the square.
